document_check.note: Document is Boudaya, Chaabene, Bouaziz, Hokelmann and Chaari (2024), 'Mild Cognitive Impairment detection based on EEG and HRV data', Digital Signal Processing 147:104399. It is an EEG+HRV MCI-versus-HC classification study, which is the modality VF-07 names for this supporter ('EEG+HRV'). The summaries.md header for Paper 83 names the same PDF file (1-s2.0-S1051200424000241-main.pdf).

cited_result: Performance of the hybrid voting classifier (SVM + GB + RF) on fused EEG and HRV time-domain, frequency-domain and non-linear features, recorded during the CERAD task, for MCI versus healthy controls: average accuracy 93.86%, sensitivity 93.87%, specificity 93.53% across CERAD tests (best 97.43% on test T1). This is the result through which the study supports VF-07's claim that temporal-dynamic features serve as MCI-discriminative signals in EEG+HRV.
tool_reason: The result is the discrimination of a machine-learning classifier built from many EEG and HRV features to label participants as MCI or healthy control, so PROBAST with the PROBAST+AI considerations applies.

domains.rationale: Diagnosed MCI cases and healthy controls were recruited separately, so this is a diagnostic case-control design. 9 of 24 recruited participants (37.5%) were then excluded on the basis of the raw data and the CERAD score. Table 1 also labels one participant inconsistently.

signalling.question: 1.1 Were appropriate data sources used (e.g. cohort, RCT or nested case-control data)?
signalling.quote: During this study, our data was gathered from 24 participants including 13 MCI (6 aMCI and 7 naMCI) and 11 HC aged from 63 to 83.

signalling.question: 1.2 Were all inclusions and exclusions of participants appropriate?
signalling.quote: Based on the collected raw data and the calculated score of the CERAD task 9 participants are excluded. Therefore, this work is limited on only 15 patients.

signalling.question: PROBAST+AI data quality: are participant group labels reported consistently?
signalling.quote: P22 F 83 HC naMCI 5 24.7 TS (Table 1 row: a participant assigned to the HC group but given an MCI subtype)

domains.rationale: All participants used the same devices and the same protocol. The features are computed algorithmically from the signals, and they are available when the model would be used.

signalling.question: 2.1 Were predictors defined and assessed in a similar way for all participants?
signalling.quote: To simultaneously record EEG and HRV data, the patient is equipped with the Emotiv Epoc X and Polar H10.

signalling.question: 2.2 Were predictor assessments made without knowledge of outcome data?
signalling.quote: Time, frequency, and non-linear features are extracted from raw EEG and HRV signals.

signalling.question: 2.3 Are all predictors available at the time the model is intended to be used?
signalling.quote: In this study, a data acquisition protocol is made using EEG and HRV signals during the CERAD task.

domains.rationale: The MCI label (the reference classification) is only called 'an MCI diagnosis'. No diagnostic criteria, diagnosing clinician, cognitive cut-offs, verification of HC status or timing relative to recording is reported.

signalling.question: 3.1 Was the outcome determined appropriately?
signalling.quote: Looked for how the MCI diagnosis and HC status were established (criteria, clinician, tests); the only statement is: 'to meet the inclusion criteria, a patient must be between the ages of 50 and 85 and have an MCI diagnosis.'

signalling.question: 3.2 Was a pre-specified or standard outcome definition used?
signalling.quote: Looked for named diagnostic criteria (e.g. Petersen, NIA-AA, DSM); none reported anywhere in the text.

signalling.question: 3.3 Were predictors excluded from the outcome definition?
signalling.quote: Time, frequency, and non-linear features are extracted from raw EEG and HRV signals.

signalling.question: 3.4 Was the outcome defined and determined in a similar way for all participants?
signalling.quote: Looked for a common diagnostic procedure applied to both groups; none described.

signalling.question: 3.5 Was the outcome determined without knowledge of predictor information?
signalling.quote: to meet the inclusion criteria, a patient must be between the ages of 50 and 85 and have an MCI diagnosis.

signalling.question: 3.6 Was the time interval between predictor assessment and outcome determination appropriate?
signalling.quote: Looked for the date of diagnosis relative to the EEG/HRV recording session; not reported.

domains.rationale: Only 8 MCI participants against a large feature set. The 3-s segments were shuffled and split 75/25, so segments from the same person fell on both sides of the split (confusion-matrix counts of 34 TP and 39 TN far exceed 15 persons). The window length, classifier choice and hybrid composition were selected on test-set accuracy. Cross-validation was also done over instances. No calibration was reported and there was no external validation.

signalling.question: 4.1 Were there a reasonable number of participants with the outcome?
signalling.quote: Our dataset includes 15 subjects who were randomly assigned to training and testing groups of 7 HC and 8 MCI, respectively.

signalling.question: 4.2 Were continuous and categorical predictors handled appropriately?
signalling.quote: A Z-score method was used, allowing to center the values around the mean

signalling.question: 4.3 Were all enrolled participants included in the analysis?
signalling.quote: Based on the collected raw data and the calculated score of the CERAD task 9 participants are excluded.

signalling.question: 4.4 Were participants with missing data handled appropriately?
signalling.quote: Looked for handling of missing or artefact-contaminated signal segments; none reported.

signalling.question: 4.5 Was selection of predictors based on univariable analysis avoided?
signalling.quote: The next phase is the preprocessing process which involves feature scaling and reduction.

signalling.question: 4.6 Were complexities in the data (e.g. clustering of segments within participants) accounted for appropriately? (AI: split at participant level?)
signalling.quote: For each test, we separated our data into 75% for the training set and 25% for the testing set. To boost the effectiveness of ML model accuracy and to reduce the rate of overfitting, we applied the shuffling strategy throughout the data partitioning process.

signalling.question: 4.7 Were relevant model performance measures evaluated appropriately (including calibration)?
signalling.quote: Various metrics such as accuracy (Acc), precision (Pre), sensitivity (Sen), specificity (Spec), and F1-score (F1-S) are used for numerical validation

signalling.question: 4.8 Were model overfitting, underfitting and optimism accounted for? (AI: test set held out from tuning and model selection?)
signalling.quote: According to the findings, the best time window corresponds to the lowest duration (i.e., 3 s) for both EEG and HRV signals.

signalling.question: 4.8b AI: was the hybrid composition chosen without reference to test results?
signalling.quote: Our hybrid ML model combines the best findings of these three models: SVM, GB, and RF.

signalling.question: 4.8c AI: did cross-validation keep each person's data on one side of the split?
signalling.quote: As regards leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) method, the model is evaluated on an instance that was left out following the training on all other instances.

signalling.question: AI: were preprocessing (scaling, reduction) and hyperparameter tuning done within training folds only?
signalling.quote: SVM with a Gaussian kernel (γ= 0.01 and C= 10), GB, and RF.

signalling.question: AI: class imbalance and its handling
signalling.quote: Our dataset includes 15 subjects who were randomly assigned to training and testing groups of 7 HC and 8 MCI, respectively.

signalling.question: AI: is the reported performance apparent, internally validated or externally validated?
signalling.answer: No (internal, segment-level only; no external validation)
signalling.quote: Finally, as stated hereabove, validations on larger datasets with additional experimentation on volunteers will be considered.

signalling.question: 4.9 Do predictors and their assigned weights in the final model correspond to the results reported?
signalling.quote: Looked for a final model specification (selected features, trained weights, tuning procedure); only the SVM hyperparameters are stated.

applicability.rationale: 15 highly selected participants (separately recruited cases and controls, 9 of 24 excluded) do not represent the population in which MCI detection would be used.
Consumer EEG headset and chest-strap HRV during a standard cognitive battery are feasible in the intended setting.
The MCI label is not defined, so whether it matches the review's MCI construct cannot be judged.

overall_rationale: Domain 1 (case-control recruitment and outcome-related exclusions) and Domain 4 (segment-level shuffled split with the same participants in training and test, test-set model selection, 8 events, no calibration or external validation) are high, and Domain 3 is unclear. The 93.86% accuracy is therefore very likely optimistic and reflects recognition of individuals at least as much as MCI status.
